theorem_title: Observations determine a target exactly when their common kernel is included in its kernel
natural_language_statement:
Let $I,X,V$ be arbitrary types with distinguished zeros in $X,V$, subtraction operations, observation maps $r_i:X\to V$ and target $q:X\to V$. Assume the maps preserve zero and subtraction, and subtraction in $V$ is zero exactly when its arguments are equal. For a selected set $S\subseteq I$, let $K_S=\{d\in X:\forall i\in S,\ r_i(d)=0\}$. Say the selected observations determine the target if agreement of all selected observations forces equality of the target. Then

$$
\bigl(\forall x,y\in X,\ (\forall i\in S,\ r_i(x)=r_i(y))\Rightarrow q(x)=q(y)\bigr)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\forall d\in K_S,\ q(d)=0.
$$

This is the positive kernel criterion for target determination. It records exactly the assumptions in the abstract subtraction-preserving system and requires no finiteness assumption on S.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.LinearBlindness.determinesTarget_iff_kernel_inclusion {Index State Value : Type}
    (system : System Index State Value) (selected : Index → Prop) :
    DeterminesTarget system selected ↔
      ∀ direction,
        InObservationKernel system selected direction →
          system.target direction = system.zeroValue := by sorry
